answer: Proof-of-stake protocols defend AI economies against Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital as a mesa of staked assets, preventing cheap identity duplication. If an agent tries to echo malicious consensus votes across multiple fake identities, it risks slashing its collateral. This pigment of economic commitment creates a high barrier to entry; an attacker must possess significant wealth to influence the network, ensuring the cost of Sybil creation exceeds any potential gain from subverting truth.
